rows.label: Section 232 — steel, aluminum, copper reinforced at 50%
rows.excerpt: 50 percent...for all aluminum and steel articles, most copper articles, and certain derivative articles of aluminum and steel, as listed in Annex I-A...applied to the full customs value of the imported product, regardless of metal content...April 6, 2026

rows.label: Section 232 — steel & aluminum 50%
rows.excerpt: President Trump is raising the tariff on steel and aluminum imports from 25% to 50%, with the higher tariff set to go into effect on June 4, 2025.

rows.label: Section 232 — autos & parts 25%
rows.excerpt: All imports of articles specified in Annex I...shall be subject to a 25 percent tariff with respect to goods entered for consumption...on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on April 3, 2025

rows.label: Section 232 — softwood lumber 10%, furniture/cabinets 25%
rows.excerpt: softwood timber and lumber...subject to a 10 percent ad valorem duty rate...upholstered wooden products...kitchen cabinets and vanities...subject to a 25 percent ad valorem duty rate

rows.label: IEEPA amendment — general goods raised to 35%
rows.excerpt: All articles that are subject to the additional ad valorem rate of duty of 25 percent under Executive Order 14193, as amended, shall instead be subject to an additional ad valorem rate of duty of 35 percent.

rows.label: IEEPA — general goods 25%, energy 10%
rows.excerpt: 25% additional tariff on imports from Canada and Mexico and a 10% additional tariff on imports from China. Energy resources from Canada will have a lower 10% tariff.

rows.label: USMCA Article 34.7 — joint review July 1, 2026
rows.excerpt: This Agreement shall terminate 16 years after its entry into force, unless each Party confirms it wishes to continue this Agreement for a new 16-year term...The Joint Review shall take place on the sixth anniversary of the entry into force of this Agreement.
